content: The text provided is a long list of references, guidelines, and expert contributions related to maternal and peripartum infections, as well as various interventions and outcomes in obstetrics and gynecology. 1. A case-control study published in PLoS Medicine in 2014 (Volume 11, Issue 7, Article e1001672) explored specific medical outcomes. The study was accessed on August 14, 2015. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) Global Strategy on Drug Resistance, available online, was accessed on August 14, 2015. 3. A 1992 technical working group report by WHO focused on the prevention and management of puerperal infections. 4. Dolea and Stein contributed to the Global Burden of Disease 2000 report, providing evidence and information for policy development. This document was accessed on August 14, 2015. 5. Morisaki et al. conducted a secondary analysis of the WHO Multicountry Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health, examining maternal and institutional factors associated with the administration of prophylactic antibiotics during cesarean sections. This study was published in BJOG in 2014 (Volume 121, Supplement 1, Pages 66–75). 6. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (Second Edition) was accessed on August 14, 2015. 7. The Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, a critical resource for evidence-based medicine, was accessed on August 14, 2015. 8. Balshem et al. outlined the GRADE guidelines for rating the quality of evidence in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2011 (Volume 64, Issue 4, Pages 401–406). 9. Practical guidelines for infection control in healthcare facilities, published by WHO, were accessed on August 14, 2015. 10. Dellinger et al. developed the Surviving Sepsis Campaign international guidelines for managing severe sepsis and septic shock, published in Critical Care Medicine in 2013 (Volume 41, Issue 2, Pages 580–637). 11. Basevi and Lavender reviewed the practice of routine perineal shaving upon admission during labor in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 11, Article CD001236). 12. WHO recommendations for the augmentation of labor were accessed online on August 14, 2015. 13. Downe et al. reviewed the impact of routine vaginal examinations during labor on maternal and neonatal outcomes in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013 (Issue 7, Article CD010088). 14. Lumbiganon et al. evaluated the use of vaginal chlorhexidine during labor to prevent maternal and neonatal infections (excluding Group B Streptococcal and HIV infections) in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 9, Article CD004070). 15. Ohlsson et al. reviewed the use of vaginal chlorhexidine during labor to prevent early-onset neonatal Group B Streptococcal infections in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 12, Article CD003520). 16. Ohlsson and Shah examined intrapartum antibiotics for known maternal Group B Streptococcal colonization in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 6, Article CD007467). 17. Thinkhamrop et al. reviewed antibiotic prophylaxis during the second and third trimesters to reduce adverse pregnancy outcomes and morbidity in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2015 (Issue 1, Article CD002250). 18. WHO recommendations on interventions to improve preterm birth outcomes were accessed online on August 14, 2015. 19. Flenady et al. reviewed the use of prophylactic antibiotics to inhibit preterm labor with intact membranes in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013 (Issue 12, Article CD000246). 20. Kenyon et al. evaluated antibiotics for preterm rupture of membranes in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013 (Issue 12, Article CD001058). 21. Wojcieszek et al. reviewed antibiotics for prelabor rupture of membranes at or near term in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 10, Article CD001807). 22. Siriwachirachai et al. examined antibiotics for meconium-stained amniotic fluid during labor to prevent maternal and neonatal infections in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 23. WHO recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage were published in 2015 and accessed online on August 14, 2015. 24. Chongsomchai et al. reviewed prophylactic antibiotics for manual removal of retained placenta in vaginal births in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 10, Article CD004904). 25. Chibueze et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies on prophylactic antibiotics for manual removal of retained placenta in vaginal births (unpublished, 2015). 26. Liabsuetrakul et al. reviewed antibiotic prophylaxis for operative vaginal delivery in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 10, Article CD004455). 27. Parsons et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the routine administration of prophylactic antibiotics to prevent infectious morbidities in women undergoing operative vaginal deliveries (unpublished, 2015). 28. WHO recommendations on postnatal care for mothers and newborns were accessed online on August 14, 2015. 29. Buppasiri et al. reviewed antibiotic prophylaxis for thirdand fourth-degree perineal tears during vaginal birth in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 10, Article CD005125). 30. Ota et al. conducted a systematic review of randomized and non-randomized studies on antibiotic prophylaxis for episiotomy repair following vaginal birth (unpublished, 2015). 31. Ota et al. also reviewed antibiotic prophylaxis for uncomplicated vaginal births in a systematic review of randomized and non-randomized studies (unpublished, 2015). 32. Haas et al. reviewed vaginal preparation with antiseptic solutions before cesarean sections to prevent postoperative infections in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 12, Article CD007892). 33. Hadiati et al. reviewed skin preparation methods for preventing infections following cesarean sections in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 9, Article CD007462). 34. Smaill and Grivell compared antibiotic prophylaxis versus no prophylaxis for preventing infections after cesarean sections in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 10, Article CD007482). 35. Mackeen et al. reviewed the timing of intravenous prophylactic antibiotics for preventing postpartum infectious morbidity in women undergoing cesarean delivery in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 36. Gyte et al. evaluated different classes of antibiotics routinely given to women for preventing infections during cesarean sections in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 11, Article CD008726). 37. Chapman et al. reviewed antibiotic regimens for managing intra-amniotic infections in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2014 (Issue 12, Article CD010976). 38. Mackeen et al. reviewed antibiotic regimens for postpartum endometritis in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2015 (Issue 2, Article CD001067).
